data.gender_notes: Luana is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'lucanus' meaning 'man from Lucania'. In Portuguese, it means 'light' or 'radiance'. The name Luana carries the meaning “Light, radiance” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Luana usually hope their child will grow to embody light, radiance and live with faith, good character and purpose.

She is a Christian princess who disguises herself as a man to save her people from invading Moors and later falls in love with her protector, Alvaro de Portugal.

historical_references.reference: Saint Luana, also known as Luna, is a 5th-century Roman martyr whose life is shrouded in legend. According to one tradition, she was a noblewoman who renounced her wealth and dedicated herself to Christ. Another tradition tells that she was a young woman who was martyred with her mother and five brothers during the Diocletian Persecution.
